text: A reported auction round is held as the round number, the reporting date, the result and the price of the round on listing and in the decision record, and a per-bid record waits for an element its owner names.
why: Legacy RWB-E4-024 reports the bids of a round, but no table, column or request element in the sources holds a bid, a bidder or a bid count, and no table may be invented.
read: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 AuctionRoundRequest and AssetSale; Physical Schema and Logical Data Model v8 listing and asset_sale; legacy RWB-E4-024 Data table.
confirm: The DB story of this service and the next version of the LDM name the element that holds a round's bids; until then AC1 passes on the round and its result and not on a per-bid record.
impact: The story is built and tested on the round and its reported result; a bid-level report is deferred and does not block wave 3.

text: The rwb-case state read, the rwb-case case-move answer, the rwb-payment payment fact and the rwb-partner vendor score are declared, built and tested against the documents and their fakes with the placeholder as their name.
why: No source publishes the operation names of the four consumed rows, and the C and I rows of this slice are empty, so the story may not wait for a named surface.
read: Architecture v5 slide 8 and slide 13; Ownership Map; TSD S5 T5.2 and T-A.1.
confirm: P3, P8 and S9 publish the names at the tag of RWB-S5-E4024-CON; the consumer adapts then and no code moves ahead of the document.
impact: Day 1 work starts on the fakes; the first real call is proven by the wave 3 harness and not by this story.

text: This legacy key owns R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50, the cancellation of an award after the payment term and the reopening of the round, because its AC2 tests them; R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-48, the term and the payment, stay with the payment-term story of FEAT-AST-18.
why: The split gives this key FEAT-AST-15 and names no owner for R-DIS-49 or R-DIS-50, while its AC2 cannot be tested without them and the term itself is another feature's.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-50; FSD Epics 3 to 8 v3 FEAT-AST-15 and FEAT-AST-18; legacy RWB-E4-024 AC2.
confirm: The build sequence confirms no second story evaluates R-DIS-49 or R-DIS-50; if the payment-term story claims them, the two stories are merged and this row is closed.
impact: One story evaluates the two rules and the other reads the award; no rule is built twice and AC2 is covered once.

text: The slice traces to FEAT-AST-15 of FSD S5 A2.15 and to the epic BRD row for FEAT-AST-15, and its PRD reference reads Pending (C1).
why: The plan carries no requirement id for this slice and the header fixes the PRD reference as Pending (C1).
read: Story rows of RWB-S5-E4024-APP and RWB-S5-E4024-CON with reqs []; FSD Epics 3 to 8 v3 feature table.
confirm: The PRD of this service allocates requirement ids and the RTM is repointed in step C.
impact: Traceability reads at feature level only; no build decision depends on it.

text: The DISPOSAL rule package is loaded in force through the service template and no DP-04 platform row is claimed by this slice.
why: The pattern set of the slice names DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only, and no source says the package load is a pattern of the story rather than a template capability.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04; the patterns of both slices; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.
confirm: The platform work of the rules kit names the dependency; if it does, the H row RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is added and the C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is recorded.
impact: The story carries no platform rules dependency and builds against the package version the template loads.

text: The round write records the round on listing and answers the sale record the round opens, whose contract, sale and price elements are completed by the accept and award stories; a cancellation is held in the sale's state element and the value is a placeholder where no element is named.
why: The published answer of the round write is the AssetSale schema with mandatory dates and a price, and R-DIS-49 cancels an award that no dedicated element carries.
read: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 API-S5-005 and AssetSale; Physical Schema and Logical Data Model v8 asset_sale DF-SAL-012 to DF-SAL-014; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-49.
confirm: The accept and award stories and the DB story name the award and cancellation elements; the API specification is amended if the answer changes.
impact: The round answer is built against the published schema with the open values marked; no sale element is invented.
